papers.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
papers.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. These phytosterols altered LNP mechanics an
papers.summary: This study shows that replacing cholesterol in mRNA lipid nanoparticles with naturally occurring phytosterols bearing C-24 alkyl substitutions changes the particles' mechanical rigidity and causes them to be retained longer in endosomes, which improves intracellular mRNA processing and transfection efficiency. The work maps structure-activity relationships between sterol chemistry and LNP performance, offering design rules for next-generation mRNA delivery systems.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Hofmeister ion effects on protein properties and their applications in food protein processing: A review.
papers.abstract: The Hofmeister series is a fundamental paradigm for ion-specific regulation of protein properties, with anions playing a dominant role. However, its molecular mechanism remains long-debated, and a systematic synthesis linking basic theory to food protein processing practices is still lacking. This review dissects the action mechanisms of Hofmeister anions from water structure regulation and ion-protein interactions, and summarizes their applications in protein extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization and structural modification. The principal finding is that the Hofmeister effect arises fr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the mechanisms by which Hofmeister series ions—especially anions—modulate protein properties through effects on water structure and direct ion-protein interactions. It then surveys applications of these ion-specific effects in food protein processing, including extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization, and structural modification. The authors highlight that the Hofmeister effect is a multifaceted phenomenon with practical relevance for controlling protein functionality in food systems.

papers.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump.
papers.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å r
papers.summary: Using cryo-EM, the authors determined structures of the SERCA calcium pump bound to two chemically distinct small-molecule activators (CDN1163 and UM-52) at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution. They identify a previously unknown allosteric binding site within the transmembrane domain and propose a mechanism by which these compounds enhance SERCA activity. This provides the first structural basis for pharmacological SERCA activation, relevant to cardiovascular and metabolic disease.

papers.title: From passive deposition to signal-guided targeting: a functional outer layer enables preferential stomatal colonization by a microbial herbicide.
papers.abstract: Foliar-applied microbial herbicides in the field face two interrelated bottlenecks: rapid viability loss caused by environmental stresses and passive stochastic deposition that restricts contact with host entry sites.
papers.summary: This paper addresses two bottlenecks in foliar-applied microbial herbicides: rapid loss of viability under environmental stress and passive, random deposition that limits contact with host entry sites. The authors describe a functional outer layer that converts passive deposition into signal-guided targeting, enabling preferential colonization of stomata by the microbial herbicide. This represents a formulation/engineering strategy to improve the efficacy and reliability of biological weed-control agents.

papers.title: Biophysically grounded deep learning improves protein-protein ΔΔG prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train-test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation,
papers.summary: The authors show that standard train-test splits of the SKEMPI2 protein-protein binding affinity dataset leak homology information, inflating the apparent accuracy of AI ΔΔG predictors; all tested models degrade under a stringent chain-level 60% identity split. They introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that fuses five residue-level biophysical descriptors with pretrained protein embeddings via cross-embedding attention, improving ΔΔG prediction under leakage-controlled evaluation.

papers.title: CoEVFold suite: User friendly pipelines to visually represent protein coevolution.
papers.abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data underlies current principles in protein folding and protein-protein interaction prediction, from which deep-learning models trained on protein sequence and structure datasets can predict protein structure. However, what is missing are user-friendly tools that enable researchers to identify and visualise coevolution, the principal signal that these MSAs encode. Here we present tools to identify and visualize coevolution, through a pipeline (CoEVFold) that uses basic direct coupling algorithms derived from GREMLIN and an input alignment of sequences from MM
papers.summary: The authors present CoEVFold, a user-friendly software suite for identifying and visualizing coevolutionary signals in protein multiple sequence alignments. It implements direct coupling analysis algorithms derived from GREMLIN, making the core signal underlying deep-learning protein structure prediction accessible to non-specialists. The suite provides pipelines to visually represent coevolving residue pairs, filling a gap in accessible tools for coevolution analysis.

papers.title: Advances in photothermal nanozymes: from rational design to multifunctional theranostic platforms.
papers.abstract: Photothermal nanozymes integrate enzyme-like catalysis with photothermal conversion, where localized hyperthermia accelerates kinetics, improves substrate accessibility, and modulates biological barriers to achieve synergistic amplification beyond monotherapies. This review systematically surveys design strategies and applications, with highlights centered on three interconnected aspects. A composition-based classification framework is first established, covering noble metals, transition metal compounds, carbon-based materials, Prussian blue analogues, single-atom catalysts, and metal-organic
papers.summary: This review surveys photothermal nanozymes, materials that combine enzyme-like catalytic activity with light-driven heating, and describes how localized hyperthermia accelerates reaction kinetics and improves substrate access to produce synergistic therapeutic effects. It organizes the field with a composition-based classification covering noble metals, transition metal compounds, carbon materials, Prussian blue analogues, single-atom catalysts, and metal-organic frameworks, and highlights design strategies and multifunctional theranostic applications.

papers.title: Chemical profiling, bioactivity, and machine learning-supported target analysis of Euphorbia macroclada extracts from aerial parts and roots.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia macroclada is used in Anatolian folk medicine, but its chemistry and bioactivity have not been compared across plant parts and extraction solvents. We extracted aerial parts and roots with ethyl acetate, acetone, 70% aqueous acetone and water. The extracts were then profiled by LC-MS/MS and tested in antioxidant and enzyme inhibition assays. UHPLC-ESI-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis showed 101 compounds, mainly flavonoids, hydrolysable tannins, coumarins, and phenolic acid derivatives. The aqueous acetone extracts had the highest phenolic content (up to 86.94 mg GAE per g, roots) and the str
papers.summary: This study compares the chemical composition and bioactivity of Euphorbia macroclada extracts from aerial parts and roots using different solvents. LC-MS/MS identified 101 compounds, mainly flavonoids and phenolic derivatives, with aqueous acetone extracts showing the highest phenolic content. Machine learning was used to support target analysis of the bioactive compounds.

papers.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry.
papers.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3 for predicting structures of host-pathogen protein-protein interactions, finding that accurate models can be retrieved by ranking on modelling confidence despite overall limitations. Using these models, the authors survey thousands of known host-pathogen PPIs to assess how prevalent molecular mimicry is and to characterize the structural modes by which pathogen proteins imitate host interfaces, including evidence of convergent evolution of interaction surfaces.

papers.title: Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures.
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to euk
papers.summary: The authors analyzed physicochemical properties across 373,779 high-confidence AlphaFold-predicted protein structures and found systematic organism-specific differences. These differences are strong enough to recover major features of the tree of life, and the signal persists even when restricting to eukaryotic proteins. This demonstrates that predicted structural data can capture evolutionary and organismal signatures at scale.

papers.title: An Integrated Ligand- and Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Strategy for the Prediction of Chemically Diverse GLP-1R Agonists.
papers.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. Peptide agonists, like semaglutide, targeting GLP-1R, remain among the most effective regulators of glucose metabolism and appetite. Nonetheless, recent reports of weight regain after treatment discontinuation sustain the interest in expanding the chemical diversity of GLP-1R ligands through drug discovery strategies. However, the structural complexity and conformational plasticity of class B1 G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) make conventiona
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper presents a combined computational and experimental pipeline for discovering chemically diverse small-molecule agonists of GLP-1R, a key target for obesity and diabetes. The authors integrate ligand-based and structure-based virtual screening to overcome the challenges posed by the receptor's conformational plasticity, then validate predictions experimentally. The approach aims to expand beyond peptide-based agonists like semaglutide toward novel chemotypes.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
papers.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular mode
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper applies reinforcement learning to a structure-based molecular generation model so that generated compounds are biased toward molecules available in make-on-demand chemical libraries. This addresses the common bottleneck of unsynthesizable generated molecules by ensuring candidates can be purchased and experimentally tested directly.

papers.title: AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi-omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactyla
papers.summary: This study integrates lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases versus paired primary colorectal tumors to identify non-histone lysine lactylation events linked to metastasis. The authors show that AARS1 mediates lactylation of GLUD1 at K503, which drives colorectal cancer metastasis via post-transcriptional reprogramming, supported by multi-omics and in vitro/in vivo validation.

papers.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.
papers.summary: This paper expands the known clinical spectrum of TUBGCP6-related primary microcephaly by describing cases with severe cortical malformations but without chorioretinopathy, a feature previously considered part of the core phenotype. The authors also provide insights into how TUBGCP6 variants should be interpreted, which matters because most prior cases carried at least one loss-of-function variant.

papers.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
papers.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. Whether and when these challenges demand more sophisticated physical models has remained an open question. Here, we address it th
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This paper extends free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, a standard tool for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction, to RNA-ligand systems, which pose special challenges like high flexibility, anisotropic electrostatics, and metal-dependent binding. The authors show that careful preparatory simulations combined with polarizable force fields can make FEP predictive for RNA targets, addressing when more sophisticated physical models are actually needed.

papers.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
papers.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. Conventional sequence
papers.summary: This review examines how enzymes can be engineered to function outside their narrow natural pH optima, a key limitation in industrial biocatalysis. It distinguishes sequence-dependent strategies, which involve mutating specific ionizable residues, from sequence-independent stabilization approaches that improve overall robustness without targeting individual positions. The paper aims to guide rational design of pH-tolerant enzymes for sectors like detergents, textiles, and biorefineries.

papers.title: CovPDB 2.0: an expanded covalent protein-ligand interactome.
papers.abstract: The rational design of covalently binding inhibitors to specifically block selected target proteins has become a common strategy in drug discovery. Such design is based on structural insights into how electrophilic ligands bind to nucleophilic residues. CovPDB v1.0 provided high-resolution cocrystal structures of biologically relevant covalent protein-ligand complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank. Here, we describe CovPDB v2.0, a substantially extended release that addresses three main limitations of the original resource. First, to reflect the numerous novel covalently binding ligands d
papers.summary: CovPDB 2.0 is an expanded database of high-resolution co-crystal structures showing how covalent ligands bind to protein targets, curated from the Protein Data Bank. The update addresses limitations of the original release by incorporating many newly discovered covalent ligands and improving coverage of the covalent protein-ligand interactome. This resource supports structure-based design of covalent inhibitors in drug discovery.

papers.title: Computational Prediction of Elbasvir as a Theoretical Candidate for PFOS-Associated Gut and Skin Shared Pathologies.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently co-occur along the gut-skin axis, yet the systemic triggers, particularly environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals like perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate network toxicology and single-cell multi-omics to propose a computational framework for the shared molecular signatures of PFOS-driven AD and IBD comorbidity. Utilizing large-scale clinical transcriptomic cohorts and machine learning, we computationally predicted the transcription factor MYC as a potential core pathologic
papers.summary: The authors combine network toxicology, clinical transcriptomic cohorts, machine learning, and single-cell multi-omics to identify shared molecular signatures linking PFOS exposure to co-occurring atopic dermatitis and inflammatory bowel disease along the gut-skin axis. They computationally nominate the transcription factor MYC as a core pathologic node and propose the antiviral drug elbasvir as a theoretical repurposable candidate. All findings are computational predictions without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therap
papers.summary: This study uses AI-based prescreening combined with molecular dynamics simulations to design peptide inhibitors targeting the WWP1 enzyme, which drives degradation of the tumor suppressor PTEN in breast cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer. The work identifies candidate peptide inhibitors as potential therapeutic agents for a subtype with few targeted treatment options.

papers.title: Conformational Plasticity of Orthosteric Pocket Enables the Discovery of a Novel PAD4-Selective Inhibitor.
papers.abstract: Peptidyl-arginine deiminase (PAD) family enzymes are pivotal enzymes that catalyze the citrullination of arginine in substrate proteins. Elevated levels of citrullinated proteins are tightly linked to the incidence of rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancers, thus highlighting PAD enzymes as important therapeutic targets. Although several PAD isozyme-selective and non-selective small molecule inhibitors have been reported over the last decade, it remains important to identify distinct ligands that may offer differentiated therapeutic potential or selectivity. Herein, we pr
papers.summary: This study investigates how the orthosteric binding pocket of PAD4 can adopt different conformations, and uses this conformational plasticity to discover a new inhibitor that selectively targets PAD4 over other PAD family enzymes. The work highlights structural flexibility of the active site as a route to achieving isozyme selectivity, which is important given PAD4's links to rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegeneration, and cancer.

papers.title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications.
papers.abstract: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short serv
papers.summary: This review surveys nanomaterial-based glucose sensor platforms, covering the detection mechanisms and highlighting their applications. It argues that nanomaterial approaches can overcome the cost, stability, and lifetime limitations of conventional enzyme-based glucose sensors, positioning them as promising tools for diabetes diagnosis and long-term monitoring.

papers.title: Minimal Mutagenesis Resurrects Human Uricase with Attenuated Immunogenicity.
papers.abstract: The human uricase (UOX) gene was pseudogenized during evolution, leaving uric acid as the terminal product of purine metabolism. Heterologous uricases can elicit anti-drug antibodies, which limit their long-term use. Here, we restored activity to a human-pseudogene-derived uricase reference through molecular-evolution-guided rational design. Sequence alignment guided the construction of reversion mutants by overlap-extension PCR and two rounds of combinatorial optimization. Structural modeling and an accelerated co-culture dendritic cell (acDC) assay were used to generate mechanistic hypothese
papers.summary: Researchers resurrected a functional human uricase enzyme from its pseudogenized evolutionary remnant using molecular-evolution-guided rational design and minimal reversion mutations. The engineered enzyme restored catalytic activity while reducing predicted immunogenicity, as assessed by structural modeling and a dendritic cell co-culture assay. This offers a potential strategy for treating hyperuricemia and gout with a less immunogenic human-derived uricase.

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This
papers.summary: This study designs PSMA-targeted conjugates that combine the Glu-urea-Lys binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties (acridine orange for nuclear delivery and triphenylphosphonium for mitochondrial delivery) to deliver theranostic radiometals to prostate cancer cells. The work uses both computational modeling and experimental validation to assess these dual-targeting constructs. It explores a strategy for improving radiometal delivery beyond standard PSMA targeting.

papers.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
papers.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. Receptor flexibility w
papers.summary: The authors built structural models of the kinase Lck bound to 62 chemically diverse AHBA inhibitors using a flexible-receptor docking method (CorrEA). Static docking to a single crystal structure failed to explain potency for many compounds, whereas accounting for receptor flexibility improved the structural interpretation of how this inhibitor scaffold is recognized. The work illustrates that a single rigid receptor conformation is insufficient for structure-based potency prediction in this system.

papers.title: Inclusion-Based Micromechanics in Nanostructured Media.
papers.abstract: The Eshelby theory supports inclusion-based micromechanics and provides a common framework for connecting microstructural heterogeneities, eigenstrains and effective material properties. The conventional formulations assume ellipsoidal shapes, uniform internal strain fields, and perfectly bonded interfaces. At the nanoscale, these assumptions are limited by high surface-to-volume ratios, surface and interface elasticity, interfacial imperfections and irregular geometries, which may substantially affect local mechanical fields and overall material response. This review summarizes recent extensi
papers.summary: This review examines how Eshelby's inclusion-based micromechanics must be extended to handle nanoscale materials, where high surface-to-volume ratios, interface elasticity, imperfect bonding, and irregular particle shapes break the classical assumptions of ellipsoidal inclusions with uniform strain and perfect interfaces. It summarizes recent theoretical extensions that account for these effects and their impact on local mechanical fields and effective material properties.

papers.title: Molecular Scale Modelling and Chemical and Mechanical Characterization of Graphene-Oxide-Reinforced Calcium Silicate Hydrate (C-S-H) Using Reactive Force Field (ReaxFF).
papers.abstract: Graphene and graphene oxide (GO) exhibit exceptional tensile strength and elastic modulus, and the functional groups on GO promote dispersion and accelerate hydration in cementitious matrices. This study uses molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the mechanical behaviour of graphene/GO-reinforced calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) at the nanoscale. A reactive force field (ReaxFF) with modified C/O parameters was developed to describe atomic interactions between C-S-H and graphene/GO. A more realistic C-S-H structure with varying calcium-to-silicon (Ca:Si) ratios was produced by remo
papers.summary: This study develops a modified ReaxFF reactive force field to model graphene and graphene-oxide-reinforced calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) at the molecular scale, using MD simulations with realistic Ca:Si ratios. It characterizes the chemical and mechanical behavior of these nanocomposites, showing how GO functional groups interact with the cement hydrate matrix. The work provides a computational framework for understanding nanoscale reinforcement mechanisms in cementitious materials.

papers.title: Tannic Acid Inhibits CaMKII-β Kinase Activity In Vitro and Displays Preclinical Anti-Tumor Activity in Ovarian Cancer Models.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is characterized by delayed clinical diagnosis, intrinsic/acquired platinum chemoresistance, and a high postoperative recurrence rate, highlighting an unmet clinical need for new targeted therapeutic strategies. Herein, we integrated pan-cancer transcriptomic profiling, clinical tissue immunohistochemistry, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, co-immunoprecipitation, structure-based virtual ligand screening, in vitro kinase activity assays, cellular viability functional assays, and SK-OV-3 xenograft mouse models to preliminarily reveal that CaMKII-β may mediate OC progression and
papers.summary: This study identifies CaMKII-β as a potential driver of ovarian cancer progression using pan-cancer transcriptomics, tissue immunohistochemistry, and functional assays. Through virtual screening and in vitro kinase assays, the authors show that tannic acid inhibits CaMKII-β activity and reduces tumor growth in SK-OV-3 xenograft models, suggesting a repurposed natural compound as a candidate targeted therapy.

papers.title: Cavity-Guided Chemiluminescent Probes for Drug-Metabolizing Enzymes: Rational Design , Activity Imaging, and Translational Applications.
papers.abstract: Drug-metabolizing enzymes (DMEs), which are crucial for xenobiotic biotransformation, profoundly influence therapeutic efficacy, drug safety, and physiological homeostasis. However, conventional analytical methods such as LC-MS/MS and fluorescence-based assays face limitations in background interference, spatiotemporal resolution, and in vivo imaging, while the structurally diverse catalytic cavities and overlapping substrate preferences of DMEs complicate isoform-specific activity assessment. In this context, chemiluminescence (CL) probes, particularly programmable Schaap-type 1,2-dioxetanes
papers.summary: This review discusses the rational design of cavity-guided chemiluminescent probes, especially Schaap-type 1,2-dioxetanes, for imaging drug-metabolizing enzymes (DMEs). It argues that tailoring probe structure to the catalytic cavities of specific DME isoforms enables isoform-specific activity assessment with low background and good spatiotemporal resolution, overcoming limitations of LC-MS/MS and fluorescence assays. The paper also covers translational applications of these probes.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of new GPR119 ligands from on-demand tera-scale chemical space.
papers.abstract: The orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR119 is involved in glucose homeostasis and is considered a promising target for the treatment of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. The recently solved structures of GPR119 in complex with potential endogenous lipid agonists, including oleoylethanolamide (OEA), provide a solid platform for 3D pharmacology analysis and structure-based ligand discovery. Here, we employed the V-SYNTHES2 approach to screen ∼3 trillion on-demand compounds from Enamine xREAL chemical space to identify several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. Structure-gu
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used the V-SYNTHES2 structure-based virtual screening approach to search a ~3 trillion compound on-demand chemical space (Enamine xREAL) against recently solved GPR119 structures, identifying several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. This demonstrates that tera-scale on-demand library screening can yield novel ligands for a metabolically relevant GPCR target.

papers.title: In Silico-Guided Screening of a High-Affinity PD-L1 Aptamer for the Construction of a Sensitive Electrochemical Aptasensor.
papers.abstract: Programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) is an essential immune checkpoint protein that plays a pivotal role in tumor immune evasion and has emerged as an important biomarker for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and immunotherapy monitoring. Aptamers have attracted increasing attention as promising molecular recognition elements owing to their high specificity, excellent chemical stability, and facile synthesis. In this study, we developed an in silico-guided aptamer screening strategy that integrates virtual library construction, molecular docking, secondary structure prediction, and structural interact
papers.summary: This study develops an in silico-guided aptamer screening pipeline that combines virtual library construction, molecular docking, and secondary structure prediction to identify high-affinity aptamers against the PD-L1 immune checkpoint protein. The selected aptamer was used to build a sensitive electrochemical aptasensor for PD-L1 detection, supporting cancer diagnosis and immunotherapy monitoring.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a ligand-aware benchmark for predicting protein-ligand binding sites at residue resolution, evaluated across three regimes: ligands with abundant training data, underrepresented ligands, and zero-shot ligands never seen during training. The framework uses a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering and evaluates a progressive three-stage modeling approach. The work highlights how predictive performance varies by ligand family and data availability, emphasizing the challenge of generalizing to unseen ligands.

papers.title: From Computational Prioritization to Material Supply: A Proposed Two-Axis Record for Marine Invertebrate-Associated Natural Products and Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Marine natural products can show biological activity while remaining difficult to identify, reproduce, or obtain in sufficient quantity. This critical narrative review examines that mismatch and proposes a linked record for each exact chemical entity-indication pair. The documented evaluation stage (E1-E4) records computational, in vitro, animal, or human evaluation; the production/access stage (S1-S5) records physical access, an executed laboratory route, controlled pilot production, good manufacturing practice (GMP) clinical manufacture, or established commercial manufacture. Neither coordin
papers.summary: This critical review proposes a two-axis framework for tracking marine invertebrate-derived natural products: an evaluation axis (E1–E4, from computational prediction to human data) and a supply/access axis (S1–S5, from physical availability to commercial manufacture). The framework aims to expose the common mismatch between compounds that look promising in silico or in vitro and those that can actually be produced in sufficient quantity, helping prioritize realistic drug development candidates.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of GTP-Enhanced Rab10 Modulators and Their Effects on Alzheimer's Disease-Relevant Cellular Phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Rab10-mediated membrane trafficking has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but pharmacological tools for investigating its function remain limited. Here, we screened more than 80 million compounds using structure-based virtual screening and prioritized five candidate Rab10 modulators ( R1-R5 ). These compounds exhibited favorable docking scores, stable modeled protein-ligand complexes in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and predicted acceptable ADME/toxicity profiles. Comparative docking against Rab5, Rab8, and Rab11 predicted preferential interactions with GTP-associated Rab10. R
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening of over 80 million compounds to identify five candidate modulators of the Alzheimer's disease–linked trafficking protein Rab10. The compounds showed favorable docking, stable complexes in molecular dynamics simulations, and acceptable predicted ADME/toxicity profiles, with docking suggesting preferential binding to the GTP-bound form of Rab10. This provides initial chemical tools for probing Rab10 function in AD-relevant cellular phenotypes, though experimental validation appears limited in the abstract.

papers.title: Effects of Graphene Incorporation on the Nanoscale Structure and Mechanical Response of PVDF Membrane Models: A Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) membranes require both suitable morphology and mechanical integrity, but changes in nanoscale geometry do not necessarily improve all loading responses. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations were used to compare pristine PVDF and graphene/PVDF membrane models constructed from five-repeat-unit oligomers. A force-driven sedimentation procedure was used to examine the effects of lateral cell size and polymer-chain number on deposited morphology. The structural indicator was a two-dimensional projected void-area fraction. Increasing polymer-chain number reduced
papers.summary: This molecular dynamics study compares pristine PVDF membranes with graphene-incorporated PVDF membranes at the atomistic scale, using a force-driven sedimentation procedure to build realistic deposited morphologies. The authors track a two-dimensional projected void-area fraction as a structural indicator and find that increasing polymer-chain number reduces void area, while graphene incorporation alters nanoscale geometry and mechanical response under loading. The work suggests that improved membrane morphology does not automatically translate into better mechanical performance across all loading conditions.

papers.title: A structure-derived contact-network responsiveness atlas of human proteins.
papers.abstract: Protein structures encode non-local contact organization, but static coordinates do not directly quantify how a contact network responds when effective stabilizing interactions are strengthened or weakened. Here we introduce Contact-Network Responsiveness (CNR), a structure-derived framework that converts residue-level protein coordinates into density-controlled and topology-corrected response descriptors. The method is structure-source agnostic and can be applied to experimentally determined PDB structures, AlphaFold models, or other predicted structures; here, human AlphaFold models serve as
papers.summary: The authors introduce Contact-Network Responsiveness (CNR), a framework that converts protein structures into descriptors of how residue contact networks respond to strengthening or weakening of stabilizing interactions. It is structure-source agnostic and was applied to human AlphaFold models to build an atlas of protein responsiveness. This provides a new way to quantify non-local structural organization beyond static coordinates.

papers.title: Comparative Binding Profiles of Co-Crystallized Ligands at Human Phosphodiesterase 1B Using Molecular Dynamics Simulations and Binding Free Energy Analysis.
papers.abstract: Phosphodiesterases (PDEs) biochemically break down cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) and cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP), which functionally regulate cyclic nucleotide signaling pathways. cAMP/cGMP signaling has been associated with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's disease (AD). The present in silico study focuses on the three co-crystallized ligands 0NY, 8HM, and 8HP bound to phosphodiesterase 1B (PDE1B), assessing structural stability via root mean square deviation (RMSD), conformational dynamics via root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), and hydrogen bonding and binding
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations and binding free energy calculations to compare how three co-crystallized ligands (0NY, 8HM, 8HP) bind to human phosphodiesterase 1B, an enzyme involved in cAMP/cGMP signaling linked to Alzheimer's disease. The authors assess structural stability, conformational dynamics, and hydrogen bonding to characterize the relative binding profiles of the three ligands. The work is a computational comparison of known ligands rather than a new experimental or methodological advance.

papers.title: Effects of Ultrasound on the Enzymatic Hydrolysis and Bioactivities of Food Protein Hydrolysates: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic hydrolysis is widely used to produce food protein hydrolysates enriched in bioactive peptides, but its efficiency can be enhanced by auxiliary technologies such as ultrasound. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of ultrasound on the enzymatic hydrolysis of food-derived protein matrices, emphasizing the degree of hydrolysis and bioactivities of the resulting hydrolysates. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase identified 55 eligible studies published between 2013 and 2026, of which 35 were included in the meta-analysis. The include
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 55 studies (35 in the meta-analysis) to assess whether ultrasound pretreatment improves enzymatic hydrolysis of food proteins and the bioactivity of resulting hydrolysates. The findings indicate that ultrasound-assisted hydrolysis generally increases the degree of hydrolysis and enhances bioactive properties of protein hydrolysates compared with conventional hydrolysis. The work consolidates evidence for ultrasound as a practical processing aid in producing bioactive peptides from food proteins.

papers.title: Diversity at the Acinetobacter baumannii K locus: towards a comprehensive database for in silico prediction of capsular polysaccharide types.
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is one of the most critical bacterial pathogens requiring novel approaches for infection control and treatment to curb the spread of highly resistant isolates. Epidemiological surveillance and the design and application of many non-antibiotic interventions require rapid and accurate prediction of diverse capsular polysaccharide (CPS) types from whole-genome sequence data. The internationally adopted CPS typing system relies on the in silico detection of CPS biosynthesis genes both in and outside the K locus (KL), utilizing a reference sequence database that is compatibl
papers.summary: This paper expands the reference database for in silico capsular polysaccharide (CPS) typing of Acinetobacter baumannii by cataloguing diversity at the K locus. The updated database improves the ability to rapidly and accurately predict CPS types from whole-genome sequence data, which is important for epidemiological surveillance and the design of non-antibiotic interventions against this highly resistant pathogen.

papers.title: Protective Effects of Spirulina on Obesity-Induced Renal Damage and Oxidative Imbalance: Computational and Experimental Study.
papers.abstract: Obesity, primarily driven by high-calorie and high-fat diets, is a major public health issue and a key risk factor for kidney dysfunction. It triggers glomerular hyperfiltration and oxidative stress, which can lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Spirulina has emerged as a potent natural agent with strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether Spirulina, a blue-green algae with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, can protect against kidney damage caused by obesity. The authors combine computational modeling with experimental work to examine how Spirulina counteracts obesity-induced oxidative stress and glomerular hyperfiltration, which are key drivers of chronic kidney disease.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Membranes Aid in Understanding Resistance Mechanism to Polymyxin B1.
papers.abstract: One of the major causes for hospital acquired infections is multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains. Polymyxins are a group of lipopeptide antibiotics used as a last-line resort for treatment of Gram-negative infections. Polymyxins initially target Lipid A's of lipopolysaccharides in the bacterial outer membrane via both electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Resistance to polymyxins in P. aeruginosa includes modification of Lipid A's to attenuate the interactions with polymyxins but to date our understanding of underlying mechanisms is still limited. This study was conducted t
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to model Pseudomonas aeruginosa outer membranes and investigate how Lipid A modifications reduce binding of the last-resort antibiotic polymyxin B1. The simulations help explain, at the molecular level, how changes to Lipid A weaken the electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions that polymyxins rely on to disrupt bacterial membranes, contributing to resistance.

papers.title: Activity-Guided Discovery and Functional Characterization of VTPPHVE, a Tyrosinase-Inhibitory Peptide from Golden Pompano (Trachinotus anak) Muscle Proteins.
papers.abstract: Marine-derived bioactive peptides are promising natural enzyme inhibitors, but their functional robustness and inhibition behavior require experimental validation. Golden pompano (Trachinotus anak) muscle proteins were subjected to ultrasound-assisted neutral protease-papain hydrolysis, activity-guided ultrafiltration, LC-MS/MS identification, and synthetic-peptide validation. The <3 kDa ultrafiltration fraction showed the highest activity (75.43% tyrosinase inhibition and 51.40% apparent Cu2+ chelation) and was selected for LC-MS/MS. Five candidate peptides were synthesized after stepwise pri
papers.summary: This study used activity-guided fractionation, LC-MS/MS, and synthetic peptide validation to identify VTPPHVE, a tyrosinase-inhibitory peptide derived from golden pompano muscle proteins. The <3 kDa fraction showed strong tyrosinase inhibition (75.43%) and copper chelation, and the synthetic peptide was functionally characterized. The work demonstrates a pipeline for discovering marine bioactive peptides with potential applications in food and cosmetic industries.

papers.title: Subtractive Genomic Approach for Identification of Pathogen-Specific Essential Genes as Target and Drug Repurposing in Major Foodborne Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Foodborne diseases pose a substantial threat to global public health and economic stability, with bacterial contamination occurring at multiple stages of the food supply chain. The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among foodborne pathogens has further complicated the prevention and treatment of these infections, underscoring the urgent need for novel, pathogen-specific therapeutic targets. In this study, a comprehensive subtractive genomics approach was employed to systematically identify bacterial key genes (bKGs) as drug targets and to explore corresponding potential therape
papers.summary: This study applies a subtractive genomics pipeline to identify essential genes unique to major foodborne bacterial pathogens (absent from the human host) as candidate drug targets, then pairs these targets with drug repurposing candidates. The approach aims to address antimicrobial resistance by prioritizing pathogen-specific vulnerabilities. It is a computational target-discovery study with limited experimental validation described in the abstract.

papers.title: AI-driven transformation of GPCR research: from structural biology to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) regulate complex pathophysiological networks and represent a critical class of drug targets, but their structural determination and ligand screening are constrained by dependence on homology templates, static conformations, and a bias toward known ligands. Artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming GPCR structural biology and pharmacology by overcoming these bottlenecks. The methodologies encompass high-precision static structure prediction, dynamic conformational ensemble modeling, ultra-large-scale virtual screening, de novo ligand design, allos
papers.summary: This review describes how artificial intelligence is changing G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) research, moving beyond template-based structure prediction and static models to dynamic conformational ensembles, ultra-large virtual screening, and de novo ligand design. It argues these AI methods can overcome longstanding bottlenecks in GPCR structural biology and pharmacology and help translate findings into precision medicine.

papers.title: Rational Design of Benzofuran-Linked Isatin Derivatives as MTDLs Targeting MAO-B and Cholinesterases: Synthesis, in silico Insights, and Neuroprotection Studies.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are multifactorial diseases associated with oxid active stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurotransmitter imbalance, leading to progressive neuronal loss. Since monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) contributes to dopamine metabolism and reactive oxygen species generation, it represents an attractive therapeutic target for anti-neurodegenerative drug discovery. This study aimed to develop novel benzofuran-isatin hybrids within a multitarget-directed ligand (MTDL) strategy to achieve selective MAO-B inhibition combined with cholinesterase inhibitory and neuroprotective a
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of hybrid molecules combining benzofuran and isatin scaffolds, aiming to hit multiple neurodegenerative disease targets simultaneously. The compounds were evaluated for their ability to inhibit MAO-B and cholinesterases, with computational (in silico) docking and pharmacokinetic analyses supporting the design rationale, and neuroprotection assays assessing their protective effects on neuronal cells. The work represents a medicinal chemistry effort to develop multitarget-directed ligands for conditions like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: PhageLysData: an evidence-aware and AI-ready dataset of phage lytic enzymes and depolymerases.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophage lytic enzymes and depolymerases are relevant to phage biology, antimicrobial development, and protein engineering, but their sequence and annotation data remain dispersed across general databases, specialized resources, genome-centred collections, and prediction-oriented datasets. We present PhageLysData, an evidence-aware and AI-ready resource constructed through reproducible multisource integration, provenance tracking, and exact-sequence consolidation. The release integrates 807,366 source observations from seven primary resources into 759,105 unique exact-sequence entities, c
papers.summary: PhageLysData is a new database that consolidates phage lytic enzymes and depolymerases from seven primary sources, merging 807,366 source observations into 759,105 unique exact-sequence entities. It emphasizes provenance tracking, evidence awareness, and reproducibility, making the data suitable for AI and machine-learning applications. The resource aims to support phage biology, antimicrobial development, and protein engineering by providing a centralized, well-annotated collection.

papers.title: Identification of potential natural PPARγ agonists via graph neural networks and integrated computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus has become a prevalent metabolic disease worldwide. Current synthetic PPARγ (Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ)agonists are associated with adverse effects, highlighting the need to explore natural compounds with potential PPARγ agonistic activity. PPARγ is a vital therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. To facilitate the discovery of natural PPARγ agonists, this study integrated graph neural network (GNN) prediction, molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, in vitro activity assessment, and molecular dynamics simulations for multistage virtual screening. Three
papers.summary: This study combines graph neural network prediction, molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, in vitro assays, and molecular dynamics simulations to screen natural compounds for PPARγ agonist activity, a target for type 2 diabetes. The multi-stage computational pipeline identified three candidate natural compounds with potential PPARγ agonistic activity, offering alternatives to synthetic agonists that carry adverse effects.

papers.title: Screening of DPP-4 inhibitory peptides derived from the skin of Takifugu bimaculatus and analysis of their inhibitory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: To address the growing global type 2 diabetes mellitus burden, dietary intervention via dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibition provides a viable approach for glycemic control. Takifugu bimaculatus skin hydrolysates exhibit favorable hypoglycemic efficacy; however, the core active components remain uncharacterized.
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes DPP-4 inhibitory peptides derived from the skin of the pufferfish Takifugu bimaculatus, aiming to explain the hypoglycemic effects of its hydrolysates. The authors screen candidate peptides and analyze their inhibitory mechanisms, positioning these peptides as potential dietary agents for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Aggregate-associated interfacial organization of sodium oleate near zircon surfaces.
papers.abstract: Sodium oleate (NaOL) is widely used as an anionic collector for zircon flotation, yet its heterogeneous organization at zircon surfaces remains insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This study investigates how sodium oleate, a common flotation collector, organizes at zircon mineral surfaces, addressing a gap in understanding its interfacial behavior. The work characterizes the heterogeneous aggregate structures formed at the zircon-water interface, which is relevant to improving mineral separation processes.

papers.title: Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics-Based Investigation of the Potential Anti-Inflammatory and Cell-Survival Regulatory Mechanisms of Dapansutrile in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive cartilage and bone destruction, and disability. Existing therapies can be limited by adverse effects and cost, and additional treatment approaches remain of interest. Dapansutrile (OLT1177) is an orally active, selective inhibitor of the NLRP3 inflammasome that has shown anti-inflammatory activity and good tolerability in early clinical studies. Whether dapansutrile might also interact with other RA-related proteins has not been examined specifically in RA. This study used c
papers.journal: Open access rheumatology : research and reviews
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to explore how dapansutrile, an NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor, might interact with proteins relevant to rheumatoid arthritis beyond its known target. The computational analysis suggests potential binding to additional RA-related proteins involved in inflammation and cell survival, hinting at broader mechanisms of action. These findings are purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Correction: Integrated AUF-UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify COX-2-targeted constituents of Shaoyao Gancao decoction.
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fchem.2026.1912431.].
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article that used AUF-UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify COX-2-targeted constituents of Shaoyao Gancao decoction. It does not present new findings; it only corrects errors in the original paper.

papers.title: AI-driven strategies for Cas12 protein design and genome editing optimization.
papers.abstract: The rise of the CRISPR-CAS system has greatly promoted the development of gene editing technology. Cas12, with its unique molecular characteristics, has become an important editing tool following Cas9. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in Cas12-related research, ranging from protein structure optimization, target design to editing efficiency prediction and off-target risk assessment. AI has demonstrated great potential in enhancing system performance and discovering new mutants. Most of these models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines, E. coli,
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied to optimize Cas12 CRISPR proteins and genome editing, covering protein structure optimization, guide RNA design, editing efficiency prediction, and off-target risk assessment. The authors highlight AI's potential to improve system performance and discover new Cas12 variants, while noting that most models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines and E. coli, raising questions about transferability to plant systems.

papers.title: Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and modulates wnt/ β  -catenin signaling and androgen receptor conformational dynamics.
papers.abstract: Dermal papilla cells regulate hair follicle growth, yet bioactive peptides that influence both pro-growth signaling and androgen receptor (AR)-associated regulation remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effects of Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) on human dermal papilla cell function and its potential interaction with the AR ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD).
papers.summary: This study shows that Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) promotes the proliferation of human dermal papilla cells, the cells that control hair follicle growth, and appears to modulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Computational docking suggests MT12 may also interact with the androgen receptor ligand-binding domain, hinting at a dual mechanism relevant to hair growth regulation.

papers.title: PARP1 and PD-L1 dual-targeted bifunctional small-molecule inhibitors: a novel strategy for dual immunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Current single-agent PD-L1 immunotherapy and PARP inhibitor combination regimens have several drawbacks, including limited response rates, mismatched pharmacokinetics, and overlapping toxicities. This research aims to discover novel bifunctional small molecules that simultaneously block the PD-1/PD-L1 axis and PARP1, with prominent selectivity for PARP subtypes, to overcome bottlenecks in triple-negative breast cancer immunotherapy.
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and evaluation of bifunctional small molecules that simultaneously inhibit PARP1 and PD-L1, aiming to overcome the limitations of combining separate PARP inhibitors and PD-L1 immunotherapies in triple-negative breast cancer. The approach seeks to improve response rates and avoid mismatched pharmacokinetics and overlapping toxicities by targeting both pathways with a single agent.

papers.title: Multitarget docking and toxicity-guided prioritisation of phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against wheat fungal pathogens.
papers.abstract: The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. Blin
papers.summary: This computational study screened nineteen phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against three fungal protein targets linked to major wheat diseases (Fusarium graminearum and Puccinia graminis). Using multitarget molecular docking combined with toxicity-guided prioritisation, the authors identify candidate plant compounds with potential antifungal activity against these wheat pathogens. The work is purely in silico and provides a starting point for experimental validation of natural-product fungicides.

papers.title: GPCRVS in the detection of target-selective molecular scaffolds based on deep learning and gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: High drug selectivity minimizes unintended interactions that cause adverse effects, decreases drug potency, and are failure-prone factors in many clinical trials due to a poor balance between drug efficacy and toxicity. Sharing similar structural folds and modes of activation, G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) may represent difficult drug targets in terms of optimization of pharmacodynamic profiles towards drug target selectivity. Here, we describe GPCRVS, a web service for GPCR virtual screening, designed to detect selective drug-like compounds. GPCRVS combines machine learning for ligand-ba
papers.summary: GPCRVS is a web service that combines deep learning and gradient boosting to virtually screen compounds for selective activity against G protein-coupled receptors, a target class where cross-reactivity is a major drug-development hurdle. The tool aims to help identify drug-like molecules that preferentially hit one GPCR over structurally similar relatives, supporting selectivity optimization in early discovery.

papers.title: Identification of novel compounds from Olea Europaea targeting hDus2 as potential anticancer agents: a molecular docking and molecular dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Leukemia, a type of blood cancer, ranks among the top causes of cancer-related fatalities. Human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2) catalyzes the conversion of uridine to dihydrouridine in the tRNA and is overexpressed in cancer cells, facilitating the translational process required for cancer cell growth. Inhibition of hDus2 reduces cancer cell growth and viability while increasing apoptosis sensitivity under stress, making it an excellent cancer target. Olea Europaea is known to be abundant in flavonoids, polyphenols, vitamins, and antioxidants, and shows immense potential in providing h
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen compounds from Olea Europaea (olive) for their ability to bind and potentially inhibit hDus2, a tRNA-modifying enzyme overexpressed in leukemia cells. The authors identify candidate flavonoid/polyphenol compounds with favorable binding affinity and stability, proposing them as starting points for anticancer drug development. The work is purely computational and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: SLC38A2-Driven Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming Promotes Hypoxic Survival in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly refractory to standard therapies, including anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab. While bevacizumab prunes tumor vasculature, it exacerbates intratumoral hypoxia, which drives a metabolically resilient phenotype that limits survival benefits. This study aimed to identify the metabolic dependencies underlying GBM adaptation to hypoxia and to evaluate whether targeting these dependencies could enhance the antitumor efficacy of bevacizumab. Methods: We analyzed the spatial distribution of key metabolites in GBM patients and orthotopic xenograft mouse
papers.summary: This study identifies SLC38A2, a glutamine transporter, as a key driver of metabolic reprogramming that allows glioblastoma cells to survive under hypoxia. By mapping metabolite spatial distributions in patient tumors and mouse models, the authors show that glutamine metabolism supports hypoxic adaptation, and targeting this dependency may improve the efficacy of the anti-angiogenic drug bevacizumab.

papers.title: Advances in injectable liposome-microspheres platforms for osteoarthritis therapy: from sustained delivery to multifunctional disease modification.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, whole-joint disorder marked by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and capsular fibrosis, affecting over 500 million individuals worldwide. Current pharmacotherapies are mainly palliative, with no approved disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs). Intra-articular (IA) injection provides direct joint access but is hampered by rapid drug clearance and short residence times. Injectable liposome-microsphere (iLMP) systems have recently emerged as integrative delivery platforms that synergistically combine t
papers.summary: This review examines injectable liposome-microsphere (iLMP) platforms for treating osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disease affecting over 500 million people with no approved disease-modifying drugs. The authors describe how these combined delivery systems address the rapid drug clearance problem of intra-articular injections by providing sustained release and potentially multifunctional disease modification rather than just symptom relief.

papers.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
papers.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and molecular dynamics to screen cyclotide peptides as potential binders of CYP19A1 (aromatase), the enzyme responsible for local estrogen production in adenomyosis. The authors identify cyclotide scaffolds that interact favorably with the enzyme's active site, proposing them as starting points for developing estrogen-modulating therapeutics. The work is entirely in silico with no experimental validation.
